obituary.text:
Robert Thomas (Tommy) Sanders Sr., 83, of Pensacola passed away on May 12, 2025. He was born in Pensacola, FL on April 21, 1942, to Joseph S. Sanders Sr. and Genevieve Nobles Sanders. One of the happiest days of his life was June 4, 1982, when he married Carmen Deloris Anderson Sanders. They were married for 42 years. Tommy retired as a Linemen from Gulf Power Company in 2003. He was a Ferry Pass Masonic Lodge Past Master, a Past Commander for the Disabled American Veterans Chapter in Pensacola, FL, and served as an Air Cargo Specialist in the Air Force during the Vietnam War, December 1965 through December 1971 when he was honorably discharged. When not engaged in various and numerous "honey-do's," Tommy had a passion for hunting, fishing, NASCAR, dad jokes, News of the Weird, and classic country, blue grass, and zydeco music.

Tommy was preceded in death by Genevieve Nobles Sanders (mother), Joseph S. Sanders Sr. (father), Daniel Burton "Danny" Sanders (brother), Royce Wayne Sanders (brother), Miriam G. Brown (sister), and Joseph S. Sanders Jr. (brother). He is survived by his wife - Carmen Deloris Anderson Sanders, son - Robert Thomas (Tim) Sanders Jr., daughter – April Carmen Harvey (Thomas James [Tom]), sister – Joan Marie Pickering (Stephen) and numerous nieces and nephews.

As a gesture of sympathy or remembrance for Tommy's passing, in lieu of plants or flowers, the family requests that a donation to Disabled American Veterans be made his honor.

David Leon Sanders, age 68, of Gurdon, passed from this life on Tuesday, February 10, 2026, at Nightengale Nursing Home in Arkadelphia. He was born on June 23, 1957, in Prescott, the son of the late Alfred Leon and Bessie Lula Brown Sanders.

David was a United State Marine Corps Veteran. He retired from the Beirne Sawmill. David enjoyed spending time with family and hunting and fishing.

He is preceded in death by his parents, one sister, Jean Jenkins, one brother, Dennis Butler, and one niece, Chrystal Sanders.

David is survived by his wife, Mary Smith Sanders, one son, Brandon Sanders (Rachel) of Gurdon, one daughter, Laura Goodman, one step-daughter, Bridget Horne of Ok, four brothers, Charles Sanders (Joyce), Eddie Sanders, Jimmy Sanders (Katie) and James Sanders, four grandchildren, Leighanne Gore, Lily Gore, Kirstin Goodman, Logan Goodman, and two great grandchildren.

Funeral services will be held at 11:00 AM on Tuesday February 17, 2026, at Welch Funeral Home in Arkadelphia with Bro. Billy Griffin officiating.

Visitation will be from 6:00 to 8:00 PM on Monday night at the Funeral Home.

Interment will be at Bethlehem Cemetery in Gurdon with Military Honors.

Pallbearers are Brandon Sanders, Charles Sanders, Eddie Sanders, Jimmy Sanders, Joseph Sanders and Phillip Mitchell.

Honorary Pallbearers are James Sanders, Shane Diehl, and Daniel Smith.

Final arrangements are entrusted the The Welch Funeral Home of Arkadelphia. Visit http://www.welchfh.net to sign the guest book and view the video tribute.

Doris Juanita (Sanders) Nobles, 82, went to be with her Lord and Savior on Saturday, February 23, 2008. She was born in Pensacola to Thorough Good and Lula Sanders and was a lifelong resident. Doris was a devout Christian and faithfully attending charter member of Ferry Pass Baptist Church. She retired from Monsanto. Doris is preceded in death by her husband, Bruce S. Nobles; her parents, Thorough Good and Lula Sanders; her brothers, J.P., Reuben, Survan, Clyde, Leonard, and Frank Sanders. She is survived by her daughters, Frances Parrish and Elaine (Dickie) Parrish of Pensacola, Karen (Ken) Saxman of Gulfport, MS and Betsy (George) Cole of Gettysburg, PA; sons, Buddy (Bea) Nobles and Kenneth (Louise) Nobles of Pensacola, Roger Nobles of LaCamp, LA; and special sister-in-law, Barbara Sanders of Jacksonville, FL. She leaves the loves and pride of her life in 17 grandchildren and 26 great-grandchildren. Visitation will be held 5 to 7pm Tuesday, February 26, 2008 at Harper-Morris Memorial Chapel. Funeral Service will be held 10:00am Wednesday, February 27, 2008 at Harper-Morris Memorial Chapel with Pastor Ken Cook officiating. Burial will follow at Roberts Cemetery. Pallbearers will be grandsons. The family wishes to express heartfelt thanks to Dr. Mark S. Boatwright and staff, the nursing staff (particularly Rebecca, LeeAnn and Dalhia) of 6 South at West Florida Hospital, and Covenant Hospice Inpatient & Palliative Care Center at West Florida Hospital, for outstanding care and compassion. A very special thank you goes to our "Sister" Judy Gates for her loving care and devotion to our Mother. The family will accept flowers or a donation may be made in her name to Ferry Pass Baptist Church, 9470 North Davis Highway, Pensacola, FL 32514. HARPER-MORRIS MEMORIAL CHAPEL is in charge of arrangements.
